The differential metabolite signature is anchored in **Eicosanoid synthesis**. The enrichment analysis identified this as the top pathway, and directional relationships among key drivers were confirmed via KEGG reaction-graph analysis.

---

The differential metabolite signature is anchored in **Eicosanoid synthesis**. KEGG reaction-graph analysis confirms that arachidonic acid (C00219) is the biosynthetic precursor of the measured eicosanoids, converting to 5-HETE (C04805) via an intermediate in two enzymatic hops, establishing arachidonic acid as the upstream driver. Arachidonic acid also converts to leukotriene A4 (C00909), linking the leukotriene and HETE branches of the pathway.

**Biological significance.** The observed elevation of arachidonic acid alongside its downstream products (5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4) is consistent with activation of eicosanoid biosynthesis pathways, which mediate inflammation, leukocyte chemotaxis, and vascular tone. [disputed by verifier]

**Limitations.** The specific fold-enrichment values, FDR statistics, and the precise number of matched compounds were not fully captured in the available tool outputs, so quantitative pathway metrics are omitted. Biological interpretations regarding COX/LOX branch switching are flagged as unsupported by the enrichment data and are not asserted here.
